sentences.text:
Petitioners have filed this petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure making a prayer for quashing of charge-sheet dated 25.10.2021.
2.
Counsel appearing for the petitioners submitted that there is compromise between petitioners and respondent No.2 and an affidavit is also placed on record.
As per said affidavit, there is compromise between the parties and now there is no dispute between them.
Complainant has received an amount of Rs. 18 lacs and he does not want prosecution of petitioners.
It has also been stated that compromise is entered voluntrarily without any fear or pressure.
Statement of respondent No.2 recorded in trial Court is also placed on record, in which it has been stated that he does not want any action against the petitioners.
3. Counsel appearing for the respondent No.2 also informed the Court regarding compromise between the parties and submitted that he does not want to prosecute petitioners.
4. Government Advocate appearing for the State opposed the prayer.
It is submitted that offence committed by the petitioners is serious in nature.
In these circumstances, petition be dismissed.

5. Heard the counsel for the parties.
6.

As per compromise agreement and statement of respondent No.2 available on record and also taking into consideration statement at bar that there is compromise between the parties, it will be in the interest of justice if prosecution against petitioners is quashed.
7. FIR is registered against the petitioners under Sections 420, 120-B of Indian Penal Code and Section 66-D of Information Technology Act.
Trial Court vide its order dated 25.10.2021 has permitted the parties to compound the offence under Section 420 of IPC and had acquitted the parties of said offence.
However, trial Court is proceeding with offence under Section 120-B of IPC and 66-D of Information Technology Act.

On going through the facts and circumstances of the case,
it is clear that complainant did not want to prosecute the accused persons.
Offence which is said to have been committed by petitioners will not affect society at large.
Offence is of economic nature.
Complainant has already stated that he had received back the money and do not want to prosecute the petitioners.
8. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, it is clear that the respondent No.2 does not want to prosecute the petitioners.
Offence is personal in nature and it will only hit respondent No.2.
Society at large will not be affected by the offence.
There is little chance of getting conviction against the petitioners, as there is compromise between the parties and offence under Section 420 IPC has already been compounded before the trial Court.
In these circumstances, no useful purpose will be served in continuing with the trial.

In these circumstances, offence under Section 120-B of IPC and Section 66-D of Information Technology Act are permitted to be compounded and proceedings pending before trial Court in RCT No. 12571/2021 (State of Madhya Pradesh vs Nitish Agrawal and others) in respect of petitioners is herewith quashed.
